2 means: run the Python backend test categories as an additional quality gate before we move on.

What it covers:
1. Unit tests: isolated function and class behavior.
2. Component tests: interactions between core modules and API layers.
3. Integration tests: end-to-end backend flows and persistence contracts.

Why do it now:
1. We already validated the frontend JS side.
2. This checks that staged generation, ATS logic, session behavior, and API orchestration still hold on the Python side.
3. It is the strongest pre-push confidence check short of full CI.

How I would run it:
1. Use the project runner in [run_tests.py](run_tests.py).
2. Target categories unit, component, integration in one pass.

What you get from it:
1. Pass/fail summary by category.
2. Immediate signal on regressions in backend behavior.
3. A better handoff point before push or Phase 5 work.

Tradeoff:
1. Slower than JS-only checks.
2. More likely to surface environment-dependent failures, but that is usually useful before merging.

If you want, I can run it now and report only the key failures (if any) plus exact impacted test files.
